note: The fuzzer entry point accepts attacker-controlled bytes as long as one byte is present.
The final byte becomes the linktype for the dead pcap handle and affects compilation context.

code: filter = malloc(Size); memcpy(filter, Data, Size); filter[Size-1] = 0;
note: The rest of the bytes become a NUL-terminated filter string completely controlled by the attacker.
The filter text is parsed into the compiler's intermediate representation.
The optimizer is invoked on the attacker-shaped IR; this is the stage associated with the reported crash state.
The optimizer can detect illegal constant expressions and abort through opt_error, which stresses the cleanup path.
Any opt_error longjmps into this handler, which immediately tears down optimizer allocations.
The cleanup routine frees the graph memory; the vulnerability hypothesis is that the same allocation can be freed twice when the optimizer's error and normal exit paths both execute.
